plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of tiny four-petaled flowers open on arching shrubs and fill the air with a sweet, heady perfume. Gardens, old farmsteads and park borders turn soft purple, and bees and butterflies gather around them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April through May, with peak bloom in May
plants.location: Chicago region and the wider Midwestern United States
plants.funFact: Although it feels like a classic American garden plant, the common lilac is native to the Balkans in southeastern Europe. Single plants can outlive the houses they were planted beside, and some survive for well over a century.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: Bottle-brush spikes of glowing orange-gold flowers rise from a dense shrub with fine, needle-like leaves. As autumn turns to winter in the Sydney sandstone country, the spikes open slowly from the base upward and become a feast for honeyeaters and other nectar-feeding birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn and winter, roughly March to August
plants.location: Coastal New South Wales, Australia (Sydney region)
plants.funFact: Each Banksia spike is a cluster of hundreds of tiny individual flowers. It is also a rich nectar source at a time of year when little else is in flower for birds and small mammals.
